title: Examples: add idempotency + safe retry patterns; log request_id; streaming cancellation guidance
author: Sabrina James
description: Context: As part of the SDK parity initiative, we’re seeing repeated customer confusion around when it’s safe to retry (especially with streaming), how to use Retry-After, and how to capture request_id for support/oncall. This PR updates the public examples to show consistent, conservative retry patterns across Python/TypeScript/Go, including idempotency key usage for non-streaming calls, request_id logging on both success and error, and explicit streaming cancellation semantics. Motivators: SUP-29505 (enterprise proxy streaming disconnects, “what do we do now?”) and INT-1182 (request_id missing from customer repros). Non-goals: We’re not changing SDK behavior here; these examples assume the new standardized defaults are available, but include explicit configuration to make the behavior visible. Summary of changes: (1) Added an 'Idempotency and retries' cookbook page with per-language snippets demonstrating safe retries for 429/5xx/network errors, with Retry-After handling where available. (2) Updated quickstart examples to log request_id (from response headers or error object) and include retry_count in logs. (3) Updated streaming examples to: treat mid-stream disconnects as non-retryable by default, surface partial output, and show how to cancel/abort cleanly (AbortController / context cancellation). (4) Added a small helper module per language in examples/ to centralize backoff + jitter logic for folks who want explicit control. How to test: run examples locally against staging (or mock server) and validate (a) request_id is always printed, (b) retries do not occur on 4xx other than 429, (c) streaming cancellation stops network reads promptly, (d) streaming disconnect yields partial output + clear guidance. Risk: Low; examples-only. The main risk is teaching unsafe patterns; reviewers: please focus on correctness and conservative guidance for streaming retry/idempotency. Screenshots: N/A (CLI output snippets included in README sections).
commits: examples(cookbook): add idempotency + retry guidance and rationale
examples(python): add safe_retry wrapper + request_id logging
examples(ts): add AbortController streaming cancellation sample + error/request_id logging
examples(go): add context cancellation + retry loop sample for non-streaming calls
docs: cross-link cookbook from existing quickstarts; tighten wording on streaming retry
notable_snippets: Python (non-streaming) safe retry w/ idempotency key: `idempotency_key = str(uuid.uuid4())` then reuse the same key across retry attempts; on error log `e.request_id` if present; only retry on 429/5xx/timeouts/connection errors; respect server Retry-After when provided.

TypeScript streaming cancellation: `const controller = new AbortController(); const stream = await client.chat.completions.stream({ ... }, { signal: controller.signal }); setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 5000);` and in the catch block: print `err.request_id ?? err.headers?.get('x-request-id')`.

Go context cancellation: `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second); defer cancel();` and for streaming, treat read errors as terminal, print request_id if available, and prompt user to restart from the last completed application checkpoint (don’t auto-retry mid-stream).
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan (review): Please make the streaming guidance more explicit: we should not recommend automatic retry mid-stream unless the caller has an idempotent workflow and can tolerate duplicates. Also please add a note on partial output semantics (what is safe to persist).

Sabrina James (author): Updated streaming sections to say: do not auto-retry mid-stream by default; instead, surface partial text and a typed error; restart is an application decision. Added a paragraph on persisting partial output only if the app can de-duplicate or treat it as draft content.

Dana Lo (review): In TS snippet, we should show how to avoid double-charging concerns: don’t retry on 400s; explicitly mention that only 429/5xx/network are retryable. Also can we log retry_count consistently?
Sabrina James (author): Added an explicit retryable set in the examples and a `retryCount` field logged on each attempt. Also added a note referencing “don’t retry on 400/401/403/404/422”.
Mateusz Zielinski (review): Go example should reuse the same idempotency key across attempts; currently it generates inside the loop. That defeats the purpose.
Sabrina James (author): Fixed: idempotency key is now created before the retry loop and reused. Added a unit-ish test for the helper ensuring the key is passed through unchanged.
Dev Patel (support): +1 on request_id. Can you also add a small callout in README: when opening a ticket include SDK version, request_id, and whether it was streaming?
Sabrina James (author): Added a “Support checklist” callout block in the cookbook + linked it from the top-level README examples section.

Wei Chen (docs): Wording tweak: ‘idempotency keys prevent duplicate side effects’ is accurate, but we should avoid claiming it prevents duplicate billing universally. Please soften and keep it scoped to safe retry semantics.

Sabrina James (author): Updated language to: idempotency keys help the platform de-duplicate repeated requests where supported; still recommend customers verify application-level side effects and log request_id for reconciliation.
release_notes: Updated Redwood examples to demonstrate safe retries w/ idempotency keys for non-streaming requests.
All examples now log request_id for faster support/oncall triage.
Streaming examples now show explicit cancellation/abort patterns and conservative retry guidance.
